graph.name: blinker-555
graph.description: Switch it on and a red LED blinks about once a second, from two AAA cells; switch it off and the cells deliver nothing.

purpose.notes: The example of the edakit handbook, chapter 18: built for oneself.

accept.HINT.bulk: no cable and no plug: the cells sit in BT1 on the board; C4 1 µF ceramic and C1 100 nF at U1, as its datasheet asks (D-6)
accept.HINT.lithium: two alkaline AAA cells, not lithium: nothing charges them (LIM.backfeed) (D-6)

notes: BT1 (Keystone 2468, 53.0 × 24.6 × 13 mm) on the bottom, the board about its size; its two PC pins are soldered on the top side
SW1 at the board's edge, its knob out over it; its terminals and pegs are soldered on the bottom – not under BT1's body
D1 on top, where it is seen
C1 and C4 close to U1's V+, C2 close to U1's DC and TH (LMC555 datasheet 11.1)

conventions.pin_reference: '<designator>.<pin>' with the pin's name or role, else its symbol number – the parts entry says which pin that is

components.label: 2×AAA holder
components.notes: Keystone 2468: two AAA cells in series, PC pins; on the bottom, soldered by hand (D-1).

components.label: Power switch
components.notes: SPDT used as on/off: common to throw_a is on; pins 4 and 5 are the frame's pegs. Through-hole at the board's edge, soldered by hand (D-1).

components.label: CMOS 555 timer

accept.HINT.thermal_copper: U1 dissipates below 1 mW (250 µA at 3.2 V, D1's 4.4 mA through DIS at 0.15 V): no copper needed

components.notes: Runs from 1.5 V. The simulation holds the phase in which D1 is lit: OUTPUT low, DC (discharge) low. R1 from OUTPUT charges and discharges C2 between 1/3 and 2/3 of VDD: f = 1 / (2 ln 2 · R1 · C2). DC is free for D1.

components.label: Timing resistor
components.notes: f = 1 / (2 ln 2 · 750 kΩ · 1 µF) = 0.962 Hz, 57.7 flashes a minute; worst case 48.0–72.4 (D-5).

components.label: Bulk at U1
components.notes: The LMC555 datasheet's minimum: 0.1 µF in parallel with 1 µF at V+ (section 10).

components.label: Control voltage bypass
components.notes: The LMC555 datasheet's layout example bypasses CV with 0.01 µF (11.2).

components.label: LED series resistor
components.notes: Sized between R-4 and R-1: from fresh cells D1 at its lowest Vf takes 4.6 mA (4.9 mA with U1, ≤ 5 mA), from cells at 2.2 V at its highest 0.52 mA (≥ 0.5 mA); 220 Ω gave 0.498 mA there (D-3).

components.label: LED (hyper red, low current)
components.notes: Specified at 2 mA: 60–150 mcd – at 0.5 mA brighter than an ordinary red 0805 LED at 1 mA (D-3).

accept.HINT.thermal_copper: D1 dissipates at most 7.3 mW, its junction 30 °C at 25 °C by the datasheet's 680 K/W

components.label: Reverse-polarity PMOS
components.notes: Drain towards the cells, source towards VDD, gate to ground: on from 1.8 V, its body diode blocks cells put in upside down (D-4).

accept.HINT.gate: no driver: the gate sits on ground through R3 and Q1 never switches – nothing rings
accept.HINT.thermal_copper: Q1 dissipates about 1 µW (4.9 mA through 65 mΩ at most)

nets.name: VBAT
nets.notes: the cells: 2 × 1.6 V fresh off load, 2 × 1.1 V used (R-1); negative with both cells upside down

nets.name: VDD
nets.notes: the cells' voltage while SW1 is on, behind Q1; RESET tied to it; a little below 0 V with the cells upside down, where U1's substrate diode holds Q1's leakage

nets.name: TIMING
nets.notes: C2 swings between 1/3 and 2/3 of VDD
